uncited: **Sparse Voxel Mipmap Pyramid:** A hierarchy built by iteratively downsampling and averaging neighbors.
**Generalized N3-tree (Octree):** Used for space partitioning and empty space compaction.
**Bricks of Voxels:** Constant-sized memory blocks storing opacity, color, and normal.
**Data Cache:** Implemented as a 3D texture for reading, bound with surfaces for writing data.
**Voxel RayTracer:** Emits data usage requests based on the current view and occlusion information.
**Central Memory/Cache Manager:** Handles structure updates and loads data from mass storage or GPU cache in response to requests.
To enrich datasets, procedural methods are used.
For noise optimization, the system mimics LOD by reusing noise computation at previous resolution levels.
Only one octave of noise is computed per level of resolution and stored in the GPU cache.
A kernel uses 1 block per node and 1 thread per child node.
The custom shader kernel samples data using `brickSampler`.
It retrieves color (channel 0) and accumulates color if opacity > 0.
To mix triangles and voxels, opaque objects are rendered first to the depth buffer to skip occluded parts.
-   **Sparse-Twice Data:** Scenes often consist of dense clusters in free space.
The octree is implicit in the mipmap levels of the 3D texture.
Rays traverse the mip-map chain instead of an octree.
Rays index into the voxel data directly because the 3D texture is a world space representation of the scene.
Quadrilinear interpolation is automatically achieved with `texture()` calls because of the mip map chain.
Bricks are spatially aligned in the scene rather than existing in an amorphous memory pool, so redundant neighbor voxels do not need to be stored.
The filtering stage (mip map generation) is straightforward when there are no redundant neighbor voxels.

-   **Time and Memory Complexity:** The system achieves real-time to interactive rates on volumes exceeding GPU memory capacities by far, thanks to efficient streaming based on a ray-casting solution.
